summary.short: FTC final rule (16 CFR Part 465), effective 21 October 2024, prohibits businesses from creating, selling or buying fake or false consumer reviews and testimonials, buying sentiment-conditioned reviews, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled review sites, review suppression and fake social media indicators.
summary.long: FTC final trade regulation rule (16 CFR Part 465), effective 21 October 2024, defines terms and bars specified unfair or deceptive practices involving consumer reviews and testimonials. Section 465.2 prohibits businesses from writing, creating or selling fake or false reviews and testimonials, and from purchasing reviews or disseminating testimonials they knew or should have known were fake or false; it exempts generalized solicitations and mere consumer review hosting. Section 465.3 (review reuse) was not finalized. Section 465.4 prohibits incentives conditioned, expressly or by implication, on reviews expressing a particular sentiment. Section 465.5 requires clear and conspicuous disclosure of material insider relationships and bars officers and managers from soliciting reviews from employees or agents. Sections 465.6 to 465.8 address company-controlled review websites, review suppression, and misuse of fake indicators of social media influence; section 465.9 is a severability clause. Civil penalties for violations require the knowledge standard of section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the front matter, Background (I), Legal Standard (II), Overview of Comments (III) and Section IV through the Relatives discussion in § 465.5. The regulatory text (Part V) and the later sections are in part 2, so no operative provisions are coded here. The preamble says 'person' is replaced by 'individual' throughout the rule (IV.A.2.b). Internal inconsistency: footnote 336 says the regulatory text of proposed § 465.5(a) referred only to the officer's relationship, while the Commission intended manager disclosure too. The preamble adopts a 'knew or should have known' standard for § 465.2(b) and (c) and states that civil penalties require actual knowledge or knowledge fairly implied under FTC Act section 5(m)(1)(A). Footnote 213 gives a maximum civil penalty of $51,744 per violation; it is not coded here. Proposed § 465.3 was not finalized. Many statements in Section III and IV summarize commenter arguments, which the Commission then rejects or accepts. Part 2 covers preamble sections IV.A.3 through IX and the regulatory text of 16 CFR Part 465 from section 465.1 through 465.9 (section 465.3 is reserved). Relation target_instrument_id is empty because no registry IDs were supplied for the FTC Act or the CRFA. Civil penalties require a rule violation, and the knowledge standard ('knew or should have known') appears in sections 465.2(b)-(c), 465.5(b)(1), 465.5(c)(1) and 465.8. The preamble cites section 465.5(c)(1)(ii)(c) while the regulatory text uses (c)(1)(ii)(C). The preamble states the rule imposes no significant new burdens but also estimates small-business compliance costs of $860.95 million (heightened-review scenario). Entity and relation sections are populated, so their section_status entries are schema-required placeholders only.

Clear and conspicuous means that a required disclosure is easily noticeable (i.e., difficult to miss) and easily understandable by ordinary consumers, including in all of the following ways:
Consumer review means a consumer’s evaluation, or a purported consumer’s evaluation, of a product, service, or business
Consumer review hosting means providing the technological means by which a website or platform enables consumers to see or hear the consumer reviews
Consumer testimonial means an advertising or promotional message

evidence.quote: Fake indicators of social media influence means indicators of social media influence generated by bots, purported individual accounts not associated with a real individual
Immediate Relative means a spouse, parent, child, or sibling.

Indicators of social media influence means any metrics used by the public to make assessments of an individual’s or entity’s social media influence, such as followers, friends, connections, subscribers, views, plays, likes, saves, shares, reposts, and comments.
Manager means an employee of a business who supervises other employees or agents
Officers include owners, executives, and managing members of a business.

Purchase a consumer review means to provide something of value, such as money, gift certificates, products, services, discounts, coupons, contest entries, or another review, in exchange for a consumer review.
Reviewer means the author or purported author of a consumer review.
Testimonialist means the individual giving or purportedly giving a consumer testimonial or celebrity testimonial.
An unfounded or groundless legal threat is a legal threat based on claims, defenses, or other legal contentions unwarranted by existing law

obligations.summary: Clear and conspicuous disclosures (defined in § 465.1(c)) must use diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers, appear in each language of the representation, be unavoidable in interactive media, and not be contradicted by other content.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies where a disclosure is required under this part.

evidence.quote: The disclosure must use diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers

obligations.summary: A business may not write, create, sell, purchase, disseminate or procure fake or false consumer reviews, consumer testimonials or celebrity testimonials that materially misrepresent the reviewer's or testimonialist's existence or experience; the business-knowledge standard applies to purchase, dissemination and procurement.
obligations.conditional_on: For purchasing, disseminating and procuring (§ 465.2(b)-(c)), the business knew or should have known of the misrepresentation.

evidence.quote: for a business to write, create, or sell a consumer review, consumer testimonial, or celebrity testimonial that materially misrepresents

obligations.summary: A business may not provide compensation or other incentives in exchange for, or conditioned on, consumer reviews expressing a particular sentiment, whether positive or negative.

evidence.quote: for a business to provide compensation or other incentives in exchange for, or conditioned expressly or by implication on, the writing or creation of consumer reviews expressing a particular sentiment

obligations.summary: Officers and managers may not write insider reviews or testimonials without a clear and conspicuous disclosure of their material relationship (§ 465.5(a)); a business may not disseminate insider testimonials lacking such a disclosure where it knew or should have known of the relationship (§ 465.5(b)(1)); officers and managers may not solicit or demand reviews from relatives, employees or agents in the circumstances listed in § 465.5(c)(1), including failure to instruct disclosure or to take remedial steps.
obligations.conditional_on: § 465.5(b)(1) and § 465.5(c)(1) apply only where the business knew or should have known of the relationship, or the officer or manager acted as described in (c)(1)(ii).

evidence.quote: for an officer or manager of a business to write or create a consumer review or consumer testimonial about the business or one of the products or services it sells that fails to have a clear and conspicuous disclosure

obligations.summary: A business may not materially misrepresent that a website, organization or entity it controls, owns or operates provides independent reviews or opinions (other than consumer reviews) about a category of businesses, products or services including its own.

evidence.quote: purportedly independent websites, organizations, or entities to review or endorse their own products

obligations.summary: Anyone may not use an unfounded or groundless legal threat, a physical threat, intimidation, or a public false accusation (made knowingly or with reckless disregard) in response to a consumer review in an attempt to prevent a review from being written or to cause it to be removed or changed.
obligations.conditional_on: The threat or accusation is made in an attempt to prevent, remove or change a review.

evidence.quote: For anyone to use an unfounded or groundless legal threat, a physical threat, intimidation, or a public false accusation

obligations.summary: A business may not materially misrepresent that consumer reviews displayed in its review section represent most or all reviews submitted, where reviews are suppressed based on rating or negative sentiment; listed criteria applied equally to all reviews are not suppression based on sentiment.
obligations.conditional_on: Suppression based on rating or negative sentiment; criteria applied equally to all reviews fall outside the prohibition.
